skill.name: desmos-graphing
skill.description: Create interactive Desmos graphs in Obsidian using desmos-graph code blocks. Use when visualizing functions, parametric curves, inequalities, or mathematical relationships with customizable styling and settings.
skill.summary: Generate accurate Desmos graph blocks for Obsidian with parser-aware equations, settings, styling, and restrictions.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

content.value_statement: Desmos blocks can fail when settings, equations, and restrictions use the wrong syntax. This skill creates parser-aware graph blocks with reliable styling and bounds.
actual_capabilities: Creates desmos-graph blocks for explicit, implicit, parametric, polar, and piecewise equations.
Adds points, labels, colors, line styles, point styles, restrictions, and hidden helper functions.
Configures graph size, viewport bounds, grid visibility, degree mode, axis labels, and logarithmic scales.
Applies the correct syntax for mathjs settings, Desmos LaTeX equations, and plain-math restrictions.
Explains common parser errors and suggests supported syntax.
Converts unsupported nonlinear polar examples into parametric forms.
limitations: Requires an Obsidian plugin that renders desmos-graph code blocks.
Does not install plugins or verify the rendered graph inside Obsidian.
Supports only the settings, colors, styles, and parser behavior documented by the skill.
Complex expressions may still require testing against the installed plugin version.

use_cases.title: Prepare classroom graphs
use_cases.description: Create labeled function plots and geometry examples for lesson notes.

use_cases.title: Visualize study notes
use_cases.description: Add styled equations, points, and restricted curves to Obsidian notes.

use_cases.title: Document mathematical models
use_cases.description: Build consistent visualizations for functions, parametric paths, and polar relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Plot one function
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Obsidian desmos-graph block for y=x^2. Use a clear viewport and label the vertex.

prompt_templates.title: Compare several functions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a desmos-graph block comparing sine and cosine from -2pi to 2pi. Use distinct colors and dashed styling for cosine.

prompt_templates.title: Graph a restricted model
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a desmos-graph block for [equation] over [domain]. Add requested points, labels, bounds, colors, and valid plain-math restrictions.

prompt_templates.title: Design an advanced curve set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a desmos-graph block showing [parametric or polar model]. Convert unsupported polar forms, add control points, and explain parser-sensitive choices.

output_examples.input: Graph sine and cosine across two periods with different styles.
output_examples.output: A ready-to-use Obsidian graph block with bounded axes, a blue sine curve, and a dashed red cosine curve.

output_examples.input: Show a quadratic Bezier curve with its control points and guide lines.
output_examples.output: A graph block containing the expanded parametric curve, three labeled control points, and dashed gray guide lines.

output_examples.input: Plot a square-root function only between zero and three.
output_examples.output: A graph block using Desmos LaTeX for the equation and plain-math syntax for the domain restriction.

best_practices: State the equation type, viewport, labels, colors, and desired restrictions.
Use mathjs syntax for settings and Desmos LaTeX syntax for equations and points.
Test complex graphs in the installed Obsidian plugin before sharing notes.
anti_patterns: Do not place LaTeX commands or symbolic pi inside restriction segments.
Do not use pipe characters inside equations or labels because pipes separate styles.
Do not request unsupported color names when a hexadecimal color is available.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates desmos-graph code blocks for compatible Obsidian plugins.

faq.question: Can it render graphs without Obsidian?
faq.answer: No. Rendering depends on an installed Obsidian plugin that supports the block format.

faq.question: Which equation types are supported?
faq.answer: It documents explicit, implicit, parametric, polar, piecewise, point, and function-definition expressions.

faq.question: Why does pi use different syntax?
faq.answer: Settings use mathjs syntax, while equations and points use Desmos LaTeX syntax.

faq.question: Can it apply domain restrictions?
faq.answer: Yes. Restrictions use plain math after pipe delimiters and must avoid LaTeX commands.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot graph errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers parser mismatches, unsupported colors, malformed labels, boundary errors, and unsupported polar equations.
